To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
pearl mice, which are lacking functional AP-3 complex, control MCMV infection in vivo independently of the production of IFNα by pDC.
the AP-2 complex does not impact the distribution and the antiviral function of DC subsets during MCMV infection, and that pDC from pearl mice are defective in IFN-α production upon viral infection.
1) AP-3 deficiency does not affect the in vivo anti-MCMV response; 2) AP-3-deficient pDC are defective in IFN-α production, but not in the control of MCMV replication
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the immune response to cytomegaloviruses in patients and in animal models.
the impact of AP3 deficiency on the production of IFN and the control of MCMV infection in vivo.
the role of the adaptor protein-3 complex in the immune response to MCMV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AP-3 has a minor impact on protective anticytomegalovirus responses.
the AP-2/3 complex has a minor effect on the control of MCMV infection in vivo.
AP-3 is not required to mount a protective antiviral immune response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AP-2 and AP-3 complexes are dispensable for the production of IFN in response to MCMV in vivo, but are required for an effective response to HSV and VSV.
AP-3 deficiency does not impact the distribution of DC populations, and that pDC from pearl mice can produce IFN-α in response to MCMV infection, but not to DNA and RNA virus infection in vitro.

AP-3-deficiency in pearl mice results in a defective production of IFN in pDC, but does not affect their distribution and function in vivo, and that an effective antiviral response can be achieved even in the absence of IFN-1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the absence of the adaptor protein AP-3 does not affect DC distribution and function during MCMV infection in vivo.
the absence of AP-3 does not affect the in vivo anticytomegalovirus immunity, and that the production of IFN by pDC is dispensable for MCMV control.
pDC can produce IFN-α in vivo, but this is not essential for the control of MCMV.
